BACKPORT: mm: split page_type out from _mapcount We're already using a union of many fields here, so stop abusing the _mapcount and make page_type its own field. That implies renaming some of the machinery that creates PageBuddy, PageBalloon and PageKmemcg; bring back the PG_buddy, PG_balloon and PG_kmemcg names. As suggested by Kirill, make page_type a bitmask. Because it starts out life as -1 (thanks to sharing the storage with _mapcount), setting a page flag means clearing the appropriate bit. This gives us space for probably twenty or so extra bits (depending how paranoid we want to be about _mapcount underflow). UPSTREAM: mm: mark pages in use for page tables Define a new PageTable bit in the page_type and use it to mark pages in use as page tables. CHROMIUM: mm: kstaled: a kswapd alternative kstaled differs from kswapd in the following respects: 1) kstaled walks page tables directly to clear the accessed bit on PTE. This allows kstaled to track the accesses of all mapped pages with even less CPU overhead comparing with the rmap. 2) kstaled stores a N-bit age, i.e., timestamp of the last access, for each page and sorts pages based on the age. This is a closer approximation to the LRU, which reduces swap refaults. 3) kstaled scans at a fixed interval to prevent thrashing. If it can't produce enough cold pages for reclaim to consume, allocation will be throttled to allow the tab discarder to take action. power: use event_count instead of wakeup_count event_count increments for a given device when pm_wakeup_event() is called by the associated driver. wakeup_count on the other hand increments only for the first device that reported the wake when in suspend/resume path. This is a problem in couple of scenarios: 1. When a wake is triggered by USB hid, wakeup count might only increments for root hub controller and not for the actual hid. 2. When a wake is triggered by a mfd device, only the mfd device wakeup count might increment and the sub-platform device's (enumerated by mfd devices) wakeup count might not increment. This change thus changes powerd code to depend on event_count rather than wakeup_count. Please look at https://lore.kernel.org/linux-pm/20190619175142.237794-1-ravisadineni@chromium.org/ for more info on why wakeup_count is not a reliable. cros-disks: migrate to generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro This CL replaces the uses of MOCK_METHOD*() and MOCK_CONST_METHOD*() macros in unit tests with the generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro, which is now the recommended way to define mocked methods with gmock. In particular, MOCK_METHOD() supports annotating a mocked method with specifiers such as 'override'. One minor change is that argument names are omitted in the argument list provided to MOCK_METHOD() in order to prevent clang-format from formatting code like `Foo* foo` into `Foo * foo`.
